mr president, although the bse crisis was of an epidemiological nature and the dioxin crisis is of a toxic nature, both have worrying common elements. both crises were caused by the introduction of recycled raw materials into animal feed and in both cases serious health problems for consumers were presented. these practices inevitably lead to the concentration and accumulation of infectious or toxic elements. the dioxin crisis has also coincided with the scandal over the use of sewage sludge in the manufacture of animal feed. in this case, the risk lies in the accumulation of heavy metals. but although we cannot make schematic analyses, i cannot ignore a comment in this context: the common agricultural policy and the world trade organisation are increasingly pushing for the pursuit of increased competitiveness as a fundamental element, which i find absolutely worrying because this kind of sacralization of competitiveness above all else is bound to lead to risky practices, such as the use of hormones or antibiotics, for example, among the raw materials for animal feed. in the european union, the precautionary principle must prevail in such cases in order to protect the health of consumers. a serious problem in relation to these issues is the poor regulation of feed manufacturing and the lack of a food policy in the european union. i would like to point out, for example, that the community institutions have not followed the recommendations and demands of parliament, which called for the ban on meat and bone meal in animal feed. the most serious problem, however, is that any ingredient which has not been expressly prohibited for the manufacture of feed is implicitly authorised. the commission should therefore draw up and make proposals for a positive list of raw materials authorized for animal feed, accompanied by a study on the impact on the production costs of animal feed in order to avoid incompatibilities with the cap. finally, mr president, i would remind the commission that it must formulate a food policy now, building on the green paper which was put into practice two years ago, and i would like to support mrs roth-behrendt's remarks on the independent food agency.
mr president, mr president-in-office of the council, mr commissioner, in recent years europe has been plunged into two major health crises caused by food: first bse in the united kingdom and then the dioxin case in belgium. this should make us think, and not just think, but take effective and urgent action. the effects of these crises have been a collective panic among consumers, unfortunate cases of affected persons and irreparable and substantial losses in cash and sound in the agricultural and food sectors. in addition, it has caused distrust among consumers, discrediting the european agri-food sector in third countries and causing headaches in the governments of the member states, and i can tell you this as the person responsible for food policy in spain. i would like to stress that this serious health crisis is being tackled by instruments which were designed for other objectives linked to the common agricultural policy, such as the standing veterinary committee, which is intended to understand animal health itself. europe must have a professional scientific committee to ensure food safety, including animal feed, which is another link in the food chain. it should have control mechanisms that allow for prevention rather than patching up after the fact, and it should have mechanisms that punish the responsibility of the member country that is attacking public health by intentionally concealing risk causes for some time. we must bear in mind that the necessary liberalisation of markets and the opening up to third countries are imposing on european agriculture and livestock a level of competitiveness that is difficult to overcome and that, unless effective preventive measures are taken, the race to lower production costs will sooner or later lead to a new similar case. legislation is very important and so is organic farming, but it is not enough. we must act with effective mechanisms. finally, i would like to draw attention to the chaotic information policy towards the commission. in the specific case of dioxin, 15 days elapsed between the communication from the standing veterinary committee and the alert network, while commissioner bonino simply stated that she did not drink belgian milk. and all this handled conveniently by the media.
council . – (fi) mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i agree in many respects with what has been said here today. the safety of consumers is vital, not just for the consumers themselves, obviously, but for the whole food chain from the field to the dining table. in fact, consumer safety is an absolutely essential aspect of an idea which has become familiar in connection with agenda 2000, that of the european agricultural model. that model includes the notion that the farmer must be able to trust in the quality of the production foods he or she purchases, such as animal feed. the dioxin crisis is also proof of this as its result is that tens of thousands of innocent farmers will suffer heavy financial losses. i agree, in this regard, with the comments of mrs grossetête and mr souchet on the european agricultural model. i would like to return to two particular comments. mr florenz raised the issue of the position of the council in this crisis. this theme was taken up by mr böge, among others. i would like to stress the fact that the council embarked on a series of measures as soon as the problem arose. the agriculture and health ministers began work on the matter in co-operation with the commission immediately. as far as the agriculture ministers are concerned, the conclusions were adopted at political level in the council in june, and now, again in terms of practical action, in the council last monday. mrs roth-behrendt mentioned the independent european food agency. this was also mentioned by mr thyssen, mr mulder and mr van dam. regarding this, i would like to state very clearly that food monitoring is the responsibility of the member states, of the regions and the local authorities. at community level we need effective control, but the office responsible for overseeing the work of the member states is sufficient for that. i would like to give my strongest assurance to mrs roth-behrendt that finland will act with complete transparency in this matter. mr president, i shall convey the messages i have heard here to my colleagues in the council.
commission . – (de) mr president, mr president-in-office of the council, ladies and gentlemen, thank you for conducting a very constructive and healthy debate on this difficult question. i would like to briefly add to certain points that have been raised. firstly, the question of the applicability of the pcb tests for pork is still open. the problem, and this particularly applies to the belgian members of parliament who have asked to speak on this issue, that we are still faced with is that as a prerequisite for using this test, parallel tests on dioxin and pcb content must be available so that a correlation can be established. in order to do this however, a minimum number of samples is required. thus far, we have received a total of eight such samples from the belgian authorities. this is far too few. as soon as we obtain the necessary results from the belgian government, we are ready to implement the required measures immediately. a second issue which has been raised by many is the question of the use of community funds to aid farmers who have been victims of this crisis. in my introductory remarks on this issue, i pointed out that in the area of market regulations, we have put in place a whole range of measures to alleviate the difficult situation in different areas. i also pointed out that we have thus far authorised eight national subsidies after notifications. however, as far as a direct community subsidy for belgian products is concerned, i have to make it clear that there is no basis in community law for doing so. ladies and gentlemen, i agree with those of you who have asserted here that the mixing together of substances which are highly contaminated with dioxins, and which is suspected here, is still a criminal act and not an animal illness. we can only pay compensation or subsidies where animal illnesses are concerned. (applause) mention should also be made of the fact that recently, there has allegedly been increased dioxin values in germany. i do not want to leave this matter hanging as that would be unfair. what is the issue here? several clay minerals were tested which are also partly used as binding agents in the production of animal feedingstuffs. in some of these clay minerals, increased dioxin values were actually found. this dioxin, ladies and gentlemen, is several million years old, and is therefore nothing new. so we must take care that these substances have also been tested where they are used in the manufacture of animal feedingstuffs. at the same time, this also demonstrates that it is not possible to have a zero dioxin value. dioxin these days is an ubiquitous substance that can be found anywhere in the world and which also occurs, unfortunately, in our countryside. what we have to prevent, therefore, is the mixing together of dioxin-containing substances or at least ensure that such substances do not enter the animal feed chain via another route in spite of sufficient controls. in this regard, i am also of the opinion, mr graefe zu baringdorf, that it is irresponsible that we do this by means of the dilution factor. that cannot be the plan. on the other hand, however, we must discuss further how we should deal with animal waste products in general. things are actually not as simple as mr böge suggests. it is also illogical, for example, that it is permissible to cook soup for human consumption from cattle marrowbone, or that the cattle marrow is even served in restaurants as a delicacy, while its use is prohibited in the animal feed industry. therefore, i am very much in favour of ruminants not obtaining their feed from materials which are animal in origin. such a black and white policy in this area is not possible, however, if we do not want to run the risk of finding ourselves with enormous difficulties in terms of waste disposal. ladies and gentlemen, a couple of small points to finish with which i consider to be important. firstly, repeated mention has been made of the issue of safety and quality requirements and an appropriate label. let me be quite clear on this point. we are not saying that if we have a quality label, we can, so to speak, permit a two-tier system as regards safety requirements. the safety requirements must be satisfied for every foodstuff; there can be no compromise on this. of course, however, there have to be other possibilities for designating particular quality accordingly. in this regard, we have the resolution from autumn ‘98, which i commented on at the time. my stance remains the same today. last point: hormone meat. on this issue i would like, ladies and gentlemen, to draw your attention to the fact that, the day before yesterday, the usa announced that they are abandoning, at least temporarily, the supply of hormone-free meat to europe since they are not currently in a position to observe the guarantees required by us. as you know, however, we have made considerable changes to our regulations so that not only are spot checks carried out on imports but that every import is scrutinised. just so you know!

counsel. - (fi) mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have the great honour today of presenting to parliament the results of the meeting of the budget council held in brussels on 16 july. i would first of all like to congratulate you on your election to parliament and wish you every success in your career, in the new challenge you are facing and in your life. the budgetary procedures for the year 2000 will inevitably be clouded by the crisis in the balkans. the commission's preliminary draft budget for 2000 had hardly been completed when it became clear that europe should make efforts to repair the damage caused by the war in the region in question and in particular in kosovo. in addition, recent events, such as the earthquakes in turkey and greece and the development of the situation in east timor, call for a rapid response from the budgetary authorities. such efforts require a high level of funding. the financing of the reconstruction of kosovo thus becomes the biggest challenge of this budgetary procedure. this became clear when we first discussed the 2000 budget with the parliament's delegation at the meeting on 16 july and this will be the main subject of the negotiations between the budgetary authorities of the union. if both parties are willing, however, it is possible to find a mutually satisfactory solution. the two institutions forming the budgetary authority presented their conception of the reconstruction of kosovo at the meeting on 16 july and the resolution of the kosovo question is essential for the success of the budgetary procedure for the year 2000. the results of the first donor conference, held on 28 july, are very encouraging in this respect. the destruction estimates, which continue to be refined, also indicate that a global funding envelope will be created in due course. at the same time, the union must meet the financing needs caused by the events we have mentioned, the earthquakes in turkey and greece and the situation in east timor, especially with regard to humanitarian aid. i would then like to present the results of the council's first examination of the 2000 budget, following the successful conciliation meeting with the parliament's delegation. our procedures are based on the new interinstitutional agreement on budgetary discipline and the improvement of the budgetary procedure, which was adopted on 6 may. it is important to respect the financing framework for expenditure set out in the new interinstitutional agreement and the detailed procedures therein for improving interinstitutional cooperation. we have examined the cases concerning the 2000 financial year in accordance with the following principles. firstly, the amendment on agricultural expenditure and expenditure relating to fisheries contracts will be examined in the autumn, in accordance with the interinstitutional agreement, so that account can be taken of the most recent estimates of the need for appropriations, without, however, excluding the reduction of appropriations for agricultural expenditure. secondly, it was decided to respect the expenditure commitments for structural items. thirdly, we are defining net centres for budget appropriations for other policies and we are trying to leave room for manoeuvre within the maximum of the categories of the financial perspective. when we examined the general line and the overall growth of the draft budget, we assumed that the union's budget for the year 2000 should be drawn up with at least the same discipline as the national budget. our procedures for administrative expenditure have been based on the following principles: growth in all expenditure in question will be limited, except in unavoidable exceptional cases, new posts will be created in limited numbers for certain areas after a thorough examination of the possibilities of reorganizing posts, and the classification of posts will not be changed or examined for reasons of career policy, except in well-justified cases. we also considered it appropriate to follow the approach used in approving the 1998 and 1999 budgets and to decide on global appropriations to be allocated to small institutions. in accordance with the principles i have just mentioned, we have agreed, by category of expenditure, on some important decisions which i shall briefly describe to you. the commission has already taken a number of decisions on the basis of the proposals contained in the white paper. we have made a firm reduction of eur 375 million in appropriations for market organizations. we have retained the appropriations in the preliminary draft budget for expenditure on associated posts and rural development. the agricultural part of the budget should be based as much as possible on current information and, accordingly, the commission should, during the autumn, update the information by a corrective to its preliminary draft budget. we shall continue to examine the expenditure relating to agriculture on the basis of this amendment in order to be able to take a final decision. as regards the structural fund programmes, we have decided to reduce the advance payment commitments for the new structural programmes to 3.5% in 2000, as against the 4% proposed by the commission in its preliminary draft budget, and payments would thus be reduced by eur 1 023 million. the reduction in question is essential to limit the growth of payment appropriations to 2.8%, the commission proposing 4.7%. this does not require any amendment of the statutes and there will be no reduction in the structural funds resources received by the member states in the years 2000-2001. as regards structural items, we also took account of the request of the european parliament in the agenda 2000 negotiations and decided to create a new budget item for the community's urban initiative. its commitment appropriations would be eur 102 million and payment appropriations just under eur 28 million. the funds allocated to commitment appropriations shall represent one seventh of the amount decided for the entire financing period. in examining expenditure on internal policies, we stressed the importance of adhering to the principles contained in the new interinstitutional agreement on budgetary discipline and the improvement of the budgetary procedure. we have taken into account in particular the estimates of the possibilities for using the appropriations and the size of the programmes accepted in the codecision procedure. commitment appropriations were reduced by eur 129 million and payment appropriations by some eur 216 million. as regards the strategy for the accession of new member states, we have reduced payment appropriations by eur 121 million. we considered that the pre-accession strategy would require fewer payment appropriations and that this would not require the amounts presented by the commission in its preliminary draft budget. as regards administrative expenditure, we have set the overall administrative appropriations for all the institutions, including the european parliament and the ombudsman, at eur 4 664 million, which represents an increase of 3.6% compared to the council's decision on the appropriations entered in the draft budget can therefore be summarized as follows: firstly, the total commitment appropriations amount to eur 92.3 billion, which means a new financial perspective, namely agenda 2000, as far as its financing is concerned. secondly, it was also a bridge in terms of the political priorities that this parliament wanted to set for the future, for the new millennium, especially in category 4 - foreign actions - where parliament made an effort to increase commitment appropriations. finally, the european parliament also increased the payment appropriations in the 1999 budget to fill the obvious gap of 1 billion in payment appropriations, a gap which had been particularly widened in the social funds. today, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are faced with four supplementary and amending budgets (brs), involving 41 transfers, and a fifth amending budget. that's a record. we also broke a famous record by taking less than 150 usually returned to the member states. but it will be useful to take this into account when we talk about the other amending budgets. as regards brs 3, my colleague mr fabra vallés will be dealing with it in more detail. i shall now turn to the fourth srs, which proposes 137 million in commitment appropriations to create the european agency for the reconstruction of kosovo, to provide important problem, mr president. when i read page 12 of the spanish version of the preliminary draft supplementary and amending budget no 4/99, i realise that we are only seeing the tip of the in the overall transfer or in a supplementary transfer this year. the commission also acknowledges that redistribution of this amount is no longer possible in category 4, and states that a mandate. so we expect the first troops to be in the area by the end of the week. the australians announced they'd be here in 24 hours. we consider it important and positive that the decision did not indonesia and, in accordance with the decision, the embargo is in force for four months, after which it will be reviewed. the legal aspects of the decision are being finalised by the competent bodies, - question no 2 by mr per gahrton (h-0407/99): the commission has not yet decided whether to grant aid to the united kingdom. subject: common defence policy of the european union the swedish prime minister, göran persson, said during the campaign for the european elections in sweden this year that a common defence policy for the european union was in fact impossible because sweden would veto the matter as soon as it came up for discussion. mr schori, then minister for cooperation, also said that there was a clear difference between what the european union understood by effective crisis management and by common defence. the european union does not intend to develop a common defence policy, but only to improve the possibilities for effective crisis management, according to mr schori. with regard to these statements, can the council state whether it is written in the texts of the treaties that the european union must develop a common defence policy? how does the council interpret the decision of the cologne summit to integrate the weu into the european union? is there a place for neutral member states in the future common foreign and security policy?
counsel. - (fi) mr president, as the honourable member knows, article 17 of the treaty on european union states that 'the common foreign and security policy shall include all matters relating to the security of the union, including the progressive framing of a common defence policy, which could lead to a common defence, if the european council so decides'. common defence is therefore presented in the treaty on european union as something that can be achieved in the future under the conditions mentioned in article iii. it also states that 'the policy of the union shall not affect the specific character of the security and defence policy of certain member states'. the cologne european council examined the european union's capabilities to carry out 'petersberg missions' under article 17 of the treaty on european union: humanitarian or evacuation missions, peacekeeping missions and combat forces missions for crisis management, including peace-building operations, where credible military means are available for this purpose. the heads of state or government committed themselves to building effective european military intervention capabilities on the basis of existing bi- or multi-party military capabilities and to strengthening european capability in this area. the general affairs council was responsible for setting the conditions and developing the measures necessary to achieve the objectives in question. it will be necessary to define detailed rules on the inclusion in community legislation of the weu activities which the european union needs to be able to fulfil the new responsibilities of the petersberg missions. the weu will therefore not be integrated as such into the european union. the necessary decisions are expected to be taken by the end of 2000. as underlined in the cologne summit resolution, this enhancement of crisis management capacity does not affect the defence solutions of each member state. the specific character of the countries which are not militarily aligned is preserved. the resolutions adopted in cologne provide for a common mission to strengthen crisis management capacity, not a reorganization of regional defence. as confirmed by the cologne european council, the common foreign and security policy also covers, under the provisions of the treaty on european union, crisis management. under the treaty, all member states have the same rights and obligations. furthermore, article 17 (3) (3) states that all member states may participate fully and on an equal footing in the planning and decision-making of the weu. the cologne european council resolutions emphasise that the successful implementation of a common european foreign and security policy implies, inter alia, that all member states of the european union, including militarily neutral member states, are able to participate fully and on an equal footing in european union operations. furthermore, decisions on crisis management missions, and in particular decisions with military or defence implications, will be taken in accordance with article 23 of the treaty on european union. member states retain the right to decide in all circumstances whether and when their national troops will be used.
counsel. - (sv) i think it is clear that as far as the future is concerned, we cannot expect categorical statements about what will happen. it is obvious that this is a possibility that could be realised with the development of the eu, but that would be the subject of specific decisions before anything is implemented. the european union must, in the present situation, devote its efforts primarily to so-called peacekeeping missions. that is what we must develop in the first place. as to what this process will lead to, nothing is certain. at the present time, it seems to me that there can be no question of a common defence.
counsel. - (sv) i think the author of the question is quite right. the fact that we have to resort to military intervention is a sign of failure. the basis of the european idea is precisely that we must strive to link the peoples of europe to one another in order to guarantee peace and security throughout the continent. when it comes to the process of enlargement of the union, the main thing is to try to involve the countries concerned in a peaceful europe, so as to prevent problems from arising in this area. i am absolutely of the same opinion, in other words i think we must direct our efforts towards measures which will prevent the emergence of crisis situations in europe or in our neighbourhood.
counsel. - (sv) it is right to say that it is very difficult to predict what might happen in such a situation. there is no legislation requiring member states to take action in such a situation. however, it is clear that we live in a union of solidarity. if one of our member states were to be attacked by a third country, we would clearly have to show solidarity. of course, such a situation, which none of us wants to happen, could then lead to reflections with various consequences. i hope that we will never have to deal with the situation mentioned in the question.

in expressing their views and presenting mrs pack's report. the assembly is aware that the commission's proposal essentially concerns the creation of an agency to implement the community reconstruction programmes, initially in kosovo and then, when circumstances permit, in other regions of the federal republic of yugoslavia, such as serbia and montenegro. it is clear that the mandate of the agency does not extend to aid to other countries from the former yugoslavia or other balkan countries, since the structure in question is the specific instrument of the european union for the reconstruction of kosovo. it is designed to ensure the necessary control of the european union over the reconstruction programme and to preserve its independence and its right of initiative in the process. the work of the agency must be clearly associated with the european union and not blend into the mass of activities of the many bodies dealing with kosovo and the region, not to stand out, but because a clear division of tasks is essential to properly identify responsibilities. the commission proposal reflects the need for an appropriate instrument for the rapid, decentralised and efficient management of reconstruction aid, which takes into account both the urgency of the situation and the exceptional nature of the efforts required. the honourable members have drawn attention to these realities on several occasions during this debate and on many other occasions. the commission's initiative is based on past experience and, in particular, on the difficulties encountered during the first phase of reconstruction in bosnia, which, as the house rightly recalled again this morning, delayed the implementation of the programmes. the commission's proposal for the creation of a european agency for reconstruction is largely based on the recommendations of the european parliament on reconstruction in bosnia. they rightly stress the need to decentralise aid management by increasing the number of staff on the ground and to provide mechanisms better adapted to the urgency of the requirements of reconstruction. i would like to mention in particular certain aspects of the commission's proposal relating to the structure of the agency. following the call for the creation of an agency made by the cologne european council, the commission's proposal is largely based on the model of existing european agencies: a structure with its own legal personality and decision-making powers, with the member states represented on a management board. such a structure will allow the reconstruction to be managed through specially designed procedures, different from those in force in the commission departments. it will make it possible to recruit staff according to the specific needs of reconstruction and for a period, as mr bourlanges said, limited to the tasks to be carried out. the agency's staff will be subject to the regulatory provisions applicable to the performance of public service tasks which the technical assistance office cannot and should not undertake. as with all other community agencies, the commission proposes that the member states be represented on the management board, in order to ensure full coordination between the activities of the european union and those of the member states in this field. this could encourage member states to use the agency to implement their own programmes. in addition, the participation of the assisting member states will make it possible, once the commission's annual programme has been adopted, to ensure that all other decisions relating to projects can be taken on the spot, without referral to the management committee composed of representatives of the member states in brussels. apart from the proposals on the agency's powers, i would like to make it very clear that the commission will continue to exercise its powers and assume its responsibilities fully. the agency will not be competent to define policy guidelines or to approve reconstruction programmes. the commission will be responsible for and take decisions on the programmes to be implemented by the agency. mr president, as the debate this morning has once again made clear, the location of the seat of the agency is a matter of some controversy in the council as well as in this house. the agency's role is to ensure that aid is delivered efficiently and promptly, which means decentralising its management and establishing genuine cooperation with the other international community actors present in kosovo. the commission has therefore chosen pristina as the location of the agency. it is the seat of the provisional administration of kosovo and all the agencies and organisations responsible for reconstruction in the region. it is kosovo that must be rebuilt. it is therefore logical that the agency should have its operational centre there, although in defending this option, i am sure that everyone will bear in mind the very convincing remarks made this morning by mr cohn-bendit about the past experience. the assembly is aware that the member states have agreed to establish the headquarters and general services of the agency in thessaloniki. the commission has reserved its position on this decision. in his view, the establishment of the agency in pristina is not a mere detail of the proposal: it is a fundamental condition for the effective management of programmes and the achievement of the agency's objectives. the commission is open to any compromise which preserves the objectives of speed and efficiency. it has already sent the presidency of the council and parliament a document in which it proposes a clear functional distribution of the services and staff of the agency between pristina and thessaloniki, with all the operational services and the director of the agency to be in pristina, at the heart of the operations. finally, on behalf of the commission, i should like to thank parliament for its amendments. the new commission will of course study them carefully. i would remind you, however, that parliament and the commission share the same objective: to optimise the speed and efficiency of the commission's efforts on the ground in kosovo for the people of the region. the newly elected commission would like to take a little time to look at the situation and your amendments, to be as sure coordination with non-governmental organisations. the budgetary transparency is another essential aspect, since parliament proposes to draw a clear distinction between contributions from the community budget and those from other sources, and to distinguish between expenditure on physical reconstruction and expenditure on institutional development. finally, mr president, the commission is in favour would be further strengthened. i am sure that we will gain a great deal from a little pause, the necessity of which is generally recognized, if we are to achieve our objective: rapid and effective aid for and with the support of the people of kosovo. - question no 34 by mr jan andersson (h-0469/99): subject: measures envisaged by the commission to combat drug addiction and prevent the use of doping substances by sportsmen the seville world championships in athletics have once again raised the issue of doping among top athletes. the widespread use of doping substances has serious consequences for sport itself, but also because top athletes are often used as role models for young people. as a result, doping among high-level athletes may increase tolerance to the use of doping products or other drugs among young people. does the commission intend, in the context of its ongoing efforts to combat drugs or in other contexts, to take measures to prevent the use of doping substances by athletes?
commission. - the honourable member asks what the commission intends to do in the fight against doping. following the statements made by president prodi to the european parliament, the commission is carrying out a thorough analysis of the situation created by the increase in doping cases in sport and is considering concrete measures that could be taken at community level. in this analysis, we take into account the resolution of your parliament of december 1998 and the conclusions of the presidency of the council following the two informal meetings of the ministers responsible for sport. we are also working closely with the member states and the council of europe on this subject in a working group which has already met on several occasions. as regards the creation of a world anti-doping agency, i can tell you, mr president, that the commission has been dealing with this issue as recently as today. we have had a first round table on the initiative of the ministers for sport. i met some of them yesterday and they told me that the commission had to act very quickly if we were to be part of this global agency as the european union. the commission is expected to take a decision on this next week. so you can see we're making giant strides on this case. in parallel with the possible accession of the union to the world anti-doping agency, we are convinced that we need a european plan, a plan which implies our responsibility, with the fifteen moving at the same pace to combat the scourge of doping. this will be the subject of the document we are preparing at the moment so that mr prodi, at the helsinki summit, can inform the heads of state and government of the measures to be taken in this field. we will then be able to propose concrete measures to be implemented in our member states from next year.
commission. - the honourable member is well aware of the problems of the fight against doping. i thank him for his contribution and would like to discuss this subject with him, because he seems to have information that i would like to take advantage of. let's get to the real question. you know, mr deputy, that the treaty of amsterdam clearly specifies the existence of european competence in this area, but it is also necessary to take account of the subsidiarity and autonomy of the sports world. the actions i would like to put before the college and parliament will therefore be actions which will have the consent of the member states and which will guarantee this autonomy. i'm also responsible for youth programs. i have already discussed this with the colleagues who deal with these matters in parliament. i am very sensitive to prevention through youth movements. our analysis has shown that in most cases it is the sporting activities which are most popular among young people. so i think that through these young people, through these movements and through sport, we can convey a lot of ideas about cooperation, fair-play attitudes and the elimination of racism and xenophobia. therefore, by following such guidelines - fair play, sport, healthy youth - youth programmes will go in the direction the honourable member wants.

- question no 43 by mr david w. martin (h-0517/99): subject: east timor: what assistance does the commission propose to provide for the reconstruction of east timor? question no 44 by mr mário soares (h-0543/99) subject: east timor could the commission indicate what action it intends to take on behalf of the european union with regard to east timor?
commission - the commission considers that humanitarian aid is a top priority in east timor. echo is resuming its €2 million humanitarian aid projects which were temporarily suspended. in addition, a series of aid projects with a budget of eur 3 million is about to be launched. if necessary, larger amounts of money - and i stress this point - can be made available for humanitarian purposes. as regards reconstruction programmes, the commission is in close contact with the world bank and the main donors with a view to developing a coherent project and avoiding duplication of donor contributions. the united nations will establish an interim administration for a period of time. the commission obviously intends to participate actively in this transitional period. a procedure has been initiated which makes a significant contribution to unamet in support of the establishment of administrative structures.
commission - let me say to the honourable member, who in the course of his distinguished career has gained far more experience in this field than anyone else in this house, that our aid seems to me to fall into three stages. firstly, immediate humanitarian aid, which is essential, particularly in view of the systematic destruction of infrastructure and transport by the militias in east timor. secondly - and this is of immense importance, i have discussed this with the secretary-general and the deputy secretary-general at the united nations - the question of the financing of the civil administration in the short and long term must be addressed. as far back as we can go, no one remembers the existence of a local civil administration. the cost of running services in east timor will be very high. that is why i mentioned the contributions to unamet. i hope that we and the member states will be able to help, as portugal has already said it would. thirdly, support for longterm development and longterm reconstruction. we are currently discussing this with the world bank. a donor meeting was held on 29 september, following which a mission will be established to examine the amount of funds needed. i want us to do what is best for east timor and not just juggle numbers. i can assure the honourable member that this is not a way of discharging our obligations to this part of the world and to this future country. for years, all the foreign ministers from europe and north america who visited indonesia had to write a note for the east timor dossier. today we must make the speeches we have made over the years a reality through the funds allocated. i hope we do so in a sensible and effective way and that we focus on the real needs.

corruption. in sum, we can say that we are now working for welfare, democracy, human rights and honesty. it should also be remembered that the starting point of the european union was the commission. - i shall not go over all the subjects we have discussed, but simply thank the speakers - or at least most of them - for their support and answer a few specific points or some of the questions put by the speakers. first question: can we, should we, do impact analyses of something like a round on the economy or the environment? i believe that in the case of economics, this is not necessary, even if it is not an exact science, because the majority of economists consider, for the reasons stated earlier, that trade liberalization is going in the right direction. this is less obvious for the environment, to the extent that the commission has taken the initiative to start an environmental impact study in connection with the round we are about to launch. so we might ask ourselves why we didn't do it for the uruguay round? we did not do it because at the time we had not thought about it, we did not have the means, and to do it today on the basis of the uruguay round would not make methodological sense. but we've already started doing it for the next round; counsel. - (fi) mr president, mrs jackson said that the politicians had concealed the fact that implementation would be costly and difficult. i do not know how the debate is going in other member states, but in my own country it is no secret that reducing emissions will require major changes. a question was asked here about the impact of emission reductions on employment. i am personally convinced that the implementation of emission reductions will create jobs on the one hand, but that it is equally certain that it will also eliminate jobs on the other. those who will find jobs may not yet know for sure, but those who are at risk of losing them know better, which is why the lobbying is unfortunately stronger on their side. many meps have raised the need for economic guidance and an environmental tax. as you know, the council has not reached a decision on this matter, so i cannot say anything on his behalf. i will simply say, and this is the finnish position, that we consider it very important that the european union should make progress towards the establishment of a common environmental taxation, and we also discussed the possibility that those member states which are willing to do so could make more rapid progress. one of the problems related to this issue is whether such a measure would be useful in situations of conflict which may arise with community competition law. in my country, for example, we have found ourselves in a situation where a national environmental tax - the first version of it - has been condemned as contrary to community competition rules. i do, however, consider energy taxes to be a means of forcing market forces to implement emission reductions and to develop new, modern and clean technologies, and i consider this extremely important. as regards ratification of the kyoto protocol, i would say that since we have not yet reached agreement on the rules of the kyoto mechanisms and on the rules for compliance with commitments, ratification at this stage would mean that we do not really know what we would ratify. when negotiations take place at international level on these issues, it is important in my view that the european union should have the advantage that it can also negotiate the conditions under which it will ratify the agreement. if the eu ratified the agreement now, it would mean that it would have little say in the negotiation of more precise rules. i agree with mr linkohr that when the european union commits itself to emission reduction targets, it must also decide on measures for member states that are not able to meet their commitments. the kyoto protocol and also the climate treaty stipulate that if a grouping of economic cooperation between states, such as the european union, is unable to achieve the objectives as a whole, the objectives set on behalf of that grouping are the responsibility of all member states, in other words if some member states cannot meet their commitments, the whole union will suffer. in conclusion, i would like to stress that the claim often made in the debate that if nothing is done, the climate will warm by two degrees in a hundred years is false. just to limit warming to just two degrees in a hundred years would require a lot of work. if we allow evolution to continue without intervention, without a determined climate policy, the climate will warm by more than two degrees in a hundred years, and therefore all the consequences will be much more dramatic.

- question no 4 by anneli hulthén (h-0473/99): the council has not yet adopted the common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the protection of employees in the event of the insolvency of their employer. subject: common method of compiling statistics on narcotic drugsthe lisbon observatory is responsible for the compilation of statistics on narcotic drugs in the member states, thus making it possible to monitor the evolution of the narcotic drug problem in the european union and to compare statistics from the member states. unfortunately, the lack of a common method of preparation is the source of many shortcomings. does the council intend to make every effort to introduce such a method and/or does it consider that other measures to make the system more functional are possible?
counsel. -sv) the council fully recognises that accurate and comparable statistics are essential for estimating the extent and nature of drug addiction and the development of drug-related crime, and for analysing the effectiveness of the methods used and the progress made. in this context, it should be noted that all member states of the union now have access to such statistics. however, it is clear that it is not enough to exchange national statistics in order to implement a european method, but that it is also necessary to ensure that the definitions on which the method will be based are comparable. however, work already undertaken in this area has revealed essential differences between national systems for collecting statistical data. member states use different indicators to describe the phenomenon of drug addiction and its effects on health, as well as the development of drug-related crime at national level. the definitions underlying these indicators also vary widely. as regards the quantity of drugs seized, some member states group drugs of different kinds, while others allocate information according to criteria that are not necessarily the same from one country to another. statistical data are collected by various types of bodies, for example by police, customs or public prosecutor's offices in general. in addition, the degree of centralisation of the systems for collecting, recording, estimating and transmitting data varies widely. it is also important to harmonise the most important epidemiological indicators gradually. the council is fully aware of these problems and in this worrying situation it can rely on the european parliament's resolution of 13 april 1999 and on the commission's communication on the european action plan to combat drugs for the period 2000-04 and on the communication of the european monitoring centre for drugs and drug addiction, the emcdda, of 17 march 1999. since its second work programme for the period 1998-2000, the emcdda has made the implementation of common indicators and the development of tools and methods for comparing interventions, legislative strategies and methods used within the union its primary objective. the aim is also to create a database of existing instruments, which will facilitate access to information and make comparisons possible. in march 1999, the emcdda repeated its message from last year, as part of an initiative by the german presidency to set up a working group to study measures to facilitate comparisons of drug statistics available to the different national police forces. a questionnaire on these statistics has been developed. the replies given by the member states will serve as a basis for the necessary development of common standards for the collection of information. the fact that the council has adopted the appropriate structures has already led to a number of conclusions, to which i referred at the beginning of my speech, on the difficulty of comparing the various national systems. our presidency is very clearly intent on supporting these efforts and ensuring that the work of recording progress in reducing drug trafficking is improved, both qualitatively and quantitatively.

- let me just say that we're making progress. we have taken steps to move forward and towards harmonized statistics. however, it is not yet possible to specify a date for the completion of all this work.

- question no 11 by mr deva is obsolete because it has been placed on the agenda of this part-session. this was communicated to the member by letter. question no 12 by pierre schori (h-0497/99) subject: cultural cleansing by the national front the library in the southern french city of orange has been the scene of a cultural purge by the national front, which has banned works deemed impure. because of a kind of fear inspired by knowledge of the past and the future, books on subjects such as egypt in antiquity and the european union at the dawn of the 21st century have been withdrawn from the shelves. this french case of infringement of freedom of expression and the unconditional right of citizens to culture is unique in the european union and in the rest of the democratic world. what measures does the council envisage to combat this form of cultural purification and to strengthen the role of libraries in promoting democracy and culture?
counsel. - (sv) the council attaches great importance to the protection of fundamental rights. according to article 6 of the treaty, the union is founded on a number of principles common to all the member states, namely freedom, democracy, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, and the rule of law. the same article states that fundamental rights must be respected in the union as general principles of community law. it should be noted, however, that the circumstances mentioned in the question are a matter for the member states. with regard to the role of libraries as a means of promoting democracy and culture, the council recalls that article 151 of the treaty on european union states that community efforts to promote cultural development in the member states, while respecting national and regional diversity, must have the following objectives: first, to promote cooperation between member states and, if necessary, to support and supplement their activities with a view to furthering and disseminating knowledge of the cultures and history of the peoples of europe; secondly, to preserve and protect a cultural heritage which has european heritage value; thirdly, to promote non-profit cultural exchanges; fourthly, to encourage artistic and literary creation, including in the audiovisual sector. on 28 june 1999, the council therefore adopted, in consultation with the european parliament, a common position on the creation of a single instrument for financing and planning cooperation in the cultural field, as required by the co-decision procedure. this programme is called culture 2000.
counsel. - (sv) as regards our fundamental values, it must be said that in this particular case the rights that should be recognised throughout the union have not been respected. however, it is still the member states' responsibility, as a last resort, to ensure the application of human rights and other fundamental freedoms in their respective territories.

counsel. - (fi) mr president, under a decision taken by the council in 1992, tax-free sales to persons travelling within the community are not in accordance with the principle of the internal market, which knows no fiscal frontiers. despite this, the council decided in 1992 to maintain the duty-free shops provisionally until the end of june 1999. the council considers that it is primarily for the member states to endeavour to mitigate the social effects in the sector in question and the regional problems in the border areas which the end of duty-free sales may entail. the community instruments available to the member states to deal with the possible consequences of the end of duty-free sales were set out in the commission communication to the council of 17 february 1999.

mr president, this budget is fundamental to european development in the years ahead. this is the first budget under the new financial perspective and its proper implementation will be a major factor in the institutional peace, without which - i would like to stress this - it will be very difficult to conduct a genuine european policy. it should be recalled that the previous parliament approved the financial perspective 2000-06 and the interinstitutional agreement in may. parliament approved them by a simple majority, but it was a clear majority. it should also be remembered that the berlin council approved the financial perspective after reaching an extremely complicated consensus, that the initial positions of the various governments were very different and that, moreover, the european commission was resigning and parliament was at the end of its term. i am saying that it is absolutely essential to defend the financial perspective now. without them we cannot guarantee, for example, the financing of the union's structural policies. it is clear that the interinstitutional agreement itself provides for the revision of the financial perspective if necessary. if the linear reduction of the union's external action is the only method the council has found for financing the reconstruction of kosovo, it is logical that the european parliament now wishes to defend these lines. in any case, we accept the compatibility between the idea of defending the application of the approved financial perspectives and the need to finance the reconstruction of kosovo by carrying out a limited revision of the financial perspectives. if that is what commissioner schreyer is proposing, it will be welcome in parliament. as regards the fisheries agreement with morocco, the commitment presented by the rapporteur at first reading has allayed the concerns of a large part of the community fisheries sector. it should be recalled that the fisheries agreement with morocco concerns almost 30 000 citizens of the union and that a large part of the fishing fleet from regions such as galicia, the canary islands and andalusia continues to operate in moroccan waters. it is only natural, and this is how the rapporteur and my group understood it, that at the beginning of the budgetary procedure we were concerned that no commitments had been made at first reading for this eur 125 million. however, by considering fisheries as a community policy whose funding comes from the treaties, we have found a formula which allows us not to reject council amendments at first reading, including those concerning fisheries, but to postpone their approval until a financial agreement is reached with the council. we would have preferred to separate the fisheries agreement from the rest of the external actions. this is tantamount to confusing two qualifications of expenditure and two problems of a different nature. however, it is also clear that the outgoing commission did not include any indication of the renewal of the agreement in its preliminary draft and, for that reason, did not include any appropriation in the reserve. if this outgoing commission had wanted to take this political step, we should not have waited for the second reading today. we will, however, have, as we have said, a political commitment from the european parliament to see that the financing of this fisheries agreement is considered a priority. this will enable us to reassure all the families and all the economic sectors which urgently need this agreement. what we have finally asked the rapporteur and the council representatives to do is to make a huge effort to negotiate. we do not want to come to the second reading with a proposal which breaks the interinstitutional agreement, because we would be left without any financial prospects. i repeat, we need the financial perspective and we need the interinstitutional agreement. but we also want european external action to be credible and therefore adequately funded. we want both of those things. and we want the member states to deal with exceptional circumstances, such as the reconstruction of kosovo, with exceptional solutions, solutions which do not limit themselves to imposing on parliament a simple linear reduction of its lines and programmes. the rapporteur-general has already made it clear that we are in a paradoxical situation and that a real solution must be found. the priorities are clear. now, gentlemen of the council, let the negotiations begin.

president of the european central bank. - it is a great pleasure for me to present the first annual report of the european central bank to the european parliament in plenary today. almost ten months have passed since the euro was successfully introduced and the european central bank took over full operational responsibility for the single monetary policy. many of us feel that the launch of the single currency has improved the quality of the european integration process. the transfer of a fundamental competence of the modern state, namely monetary policy, to a truly european and independent organisation such as the ecb, must be regarded as a historic event marking an unprecedented advance in economic and political integration within the european union. the smooth transition to this new era of european integration and the successful operational launch of the ecb were the culmination of several years of intensive and painstaking preparatory work. the ecb's annual report gives a detailed account of the latest work carried out by the european system on the eve of the introduction of the single currency, as well as of the main economic and monetary developments in the european union in 1998 and in the first few weeks of 1999. since the information in the annual report speaks for itself, it might be more useful if i focused my remarks here and now on some of the points made in the motion for a resolution by your committee on economic and monetary affairs, after which i shall be happy to answer any questions you may have. i would like to begin by commenting on the ecb's accountability to the european parliament. the treaty establishing the european community contains several provisions to ensure the democratic accountability of the ecb, one of the most important of which is certainly the presentation of the annual report to the european parliament and the council of the european union. however, beyond this annual exercise, the ecb and the european parliament have had various other contacts. i shall first mention a form of contact which is perhaps the most important, namely the regular hearings organised by the economic and monetary affairs committee. in the context of these hearings, which are held quarterly in accordance with parliament's rules of procedure, i give detailed explanations of our assessment of current economic and monetary developments and the decisions taken by the ecb. the transcripts of these hearings are available on the website of the european parliament and on the ecb's website. in addition, the european parliament invited members of the executive board and ecb officials to participate in additional hearings on a number of specific topics, including the external representation of the european system, the preparation of euro banknotes and statistical data. the ecb also had the opportunity to welcome delegations of members of the european parliament's economic and monetary affairs committee to its headquarters in frankfurt. we value these visits very much and will continue to welcome them with pleasure. however, as these visits to the ecb's premises are less formal in nature, it goes without saying that they should be seen as a complementary tool for communication between the two institutions and not as a substitute for regular hearings in the european parliament. in developing its communication policy, the central bank decided to go beyond the transparency requirements laid down in the treaty. thus, whereas the treaty requires the bank to publish a report on its activities every three months, the bank has decided to publish such a report every month, the monthly bulletin, which explains in detail economic and monetary developments. in addition, the bank regularly uses several other communication tools. i will mention first of all the lengthy press conferences that the vice-president and i hold each month immediately after the first meeting of the board of governors, the transcript of which, including the transcript of the question and answer session, is also available on the bank's website. you are of course aware of the wide range of publications of the bank on specific subjects within its fields of competence. our communication policy clearly gives priority to maintaining and strengthening the credibility of the european system and confidence in the euro, both of which are essential for the proper conduct of monetary policy. in this context, it should never be forgotten that the governing council has a collegial responsibility and that all its decisions must be communicated to the public in a clear and consistent manner. it is particularly important for a central bank operating in a monetary union of several countries to speak in a common language. contradictory information on the ecb's decisions and motives could create unjustified expectations on the part of the market and cause confusion, which is contrary to the very objective of transparency in the conduct of monetary policy. i would point out that the information provided at the press conferences immediately following the meetings of the board of governors, as well as the analyses contained in the bank's monthly bulletin and other communication tools, are very similar in substance to what is found in the summary reports. in view of the wide range of publicly available information published by the bank, i am firmly convinced that the bank has nothing to envy to other central banks in the area of transparency. in this connection, i should also like to say a few words about the request for the ecb to publish its internal forecasts. firstly, it is clear that it would be premature to consider such an initiative, given that the european system - that is to say the ecb and the 11 national central banks - has not yet acquired all the necessary experience in the field of forecasting. it will take some time before we can be sure that we have all the technical aspects under control and can consider publishing forecasts without compromising the ecb's credibility. i am convinced, however, that we shall achieve this within the next year. i will then stress that the role of the ecb's internal forecasts in the decision-making process should not be overestimated. these forecasts are only one piece of information available to the governing council, but they are certainly not the only one. the role of our forecasts in the context of the monetary strategy of the european system is therefore different from the role of inflation forecasts in a strategy specifically targeting inflation. finally, i would remind you that the monthly bulletin - especially in its quarterly compiled version - offers a longer-term analysis, including prospects for price developments. the ecb was also asked to publish a summary of national data for the countries participating in the euro area. we believe, however, that it would be misleading to publish such data, since the single monetary policy must remain independent of the specific situation of individual countries. the european system must, on the contrary, look at the euro area as a whole in order to assess the economic situation in general and the prospects for price stability in particular. the publication by the ecb of a detailed report for each euro area country would run counter to this euro area-wide overview required for the conduct, negotiation and design of monetary policy. it is, however, true that the national central banks of the european system continue to publish their own more or less detailed reports on national economic and financial developments at regular intervals. i should now like to touch briefly on another aspect which i know is at the heart of the european parliament's concerns, namely the contribution of monetary policy to the general economic policies in the community. the treaty establishes a fundamentally sound allocation of policy objectives and instruments between the monetary authorities and the governmental authorities of europe. the european system is responsible for maintaining price stability. to this end, it has adopted a long-term monetary policy strategy and it responds swiftly to threats to price stability. the treaty also states that, without prejudice to the objective of price stability, the european system shall support the general economic policies in the community. we are firmly convinced that by maintaining price stability, monetary policy contributes as much as possible to achieving a high level of output and employment in the medium term. price stability has a beneficial influence on overall economic performance, including growth and employment prospects. this influence is exercised in various ways, including the following. first, in an environment of price stability, the allocation of resources by market mechanisms according to their optimal use is more efficient. markets function best when the corresponding price signals are not distorted by fluctuations in the general price level. secondly, in a climate of price stability, the risk of inflation in interest rates, in particular long-term interest rates, is reduced, which improves the conditions for financing investment. thirdly, sustainable price stability promotes greater social justice and helps to protect the most vulnerable elements of our society, such as pensioners and the unemployed, who depend on fixed incomes and who do not have other assets, such as property or shares, to offset the cost of inflation. it is generally accepted that there is no causal link in the long run between price stability and economic growth. attempts to exploit monetary policy to push real economic activity above its sustainable level will only result in ever higher inflation in the long run, without accelerating economic growth. such a strategy would, however, negate the beneficial effect of price stability which i have just described and would therefore jeopardize the medium-term prospects for growth and employment. while the role of monetary policy in contributing to price stability should not be overlooked, it is clear that it cannot solve the serious problem of structural unemployment in the euro area. other sectors have the necessary instruments and are therefore responsible for solving structural problems. there is no doubt that decisive action in this area is needed to improve the prospects for growth and employment. sound public finances contribute to strengthening the conditions for price stability and to achieving strong and sustainable growth that creates jobs. in this context, the stability and growth pact creates the right incentives for sound and prudent fiscal policies in all participating member states. in addition, structural reforms in labour and goods markets, combined with moderate wage cost developments, are the best way to tackle the roots of the high unemployment rate in europe. the clear division of political powers i have just described strengthens the credibility of monetary and economic policies in europe, increases transparency and facilitates accountability. it provides the motivation needed by policy-makers in different sectors. if all the parties concerned respect this fundamental division of powers and act accordingly, the achievement of the objectives common to all sectors will be the inevitable result of their individual policy choices. in this respect, the ess supports the idea of a dialogue between monetary policy and other policy sectors in the form of an open exchange of information. however, such a dialogue should not be confused with any attempt to coordinate policies ex ante, in order to establish a degree of policy mix in which the fundamental responsibilities i have described would be lost. such coordination would tend to shift responsibilities, reduce the transparency of the policy framework in the eyes of the public and increase the doubts about policy action, thus potentially threatening to destabilise the economy. finally, the debate on a balanced and appropriate policy mix should not be used to divert attention from the structural reforms we so urgently need to solve the serious problem of structural unemployment in the euro area. another point raised by your committee is the contribution of the ecb to financial stability and, in particular, the question of the emergency provision of liquidity to failing financial institutions. let me give you the main points of our position on this matter. the principle prevailing within the european system with regard to the emergency provision of liquidity to individual financial institutions is that the competent national central bank is responsible for providing such assistance to institutions operating within its jurisdiction, provided that the ecb is, where appropriate, informed in a timely manner. in addition, in the case of operations linked to the single monetary policy, the decision-making bodies of the european system shall participate in the assessment of the compatibility of the envisaged operations with the objective of monetary stability. in the event of a widespread liquidity crisis resulting, for example, from a blockage in the payment system, there should be direct intervention by the european system. as far as the markets are concerned, we think it is enough for them to know that the capacity and the will to intervene properly exist if the need really arises. central banks are not in the habit of disclosing the terms and conditions of their emergency liquidity provision practices. thus, and this is characteristic, you will not find any official document describing the conditions governing the provision of emergency liquidity or the procedures to be followed. in fact, ex ante commitments would be counterproductive in this case, as they would limit the central bank's ability to react to contain systemic disruptions that are unforeseen in nature. this strategy of constructive ambiguity also helps to contain a related problem, that of moral hazard. finally, i would like to address another problem which the european parliament has also raised on several occasions, namely that of crossborder payments of small amounts in the euro area. the ecb is aware of the criticisms made of the inefficiency and high costs associated with the processing of such payments; it fully shares the concerns expressed by the european parliament in this regard. the current situation is particularly worrying in terms of crossborder transfers; the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to apply the same rules to crossborder credit card payments. you are aware that one of the main tasks assigned to the european system by the treaty is to promote the smooth operation of payment systems. however, central banks generally intervene less in small-value payment systems than in large-value payment systems, mainly because in the former case the risks likely to affect the whole system are considerably lower. however, the european system is concerned about the efficiency problems associated with crossborder payments of small amounts. at present, the performance of small cross-border payment systems is far below the policy objectives of economic and monetary union, and even the expectations of citizens and many small businesses. after the introduction of euro coins and banknotes on 1 january 2002, differences in the quality of service for national and crossborder payments within the euro area will become even more pronounced. in this context, the ecb strongly supports the idea of creating a single payment area in order to reap the full benefits of the single currency. in order to send a clear signal to the banking industry and to the public, the ecb published in september a number of objectives which it would like to see the industry achieve and which should help to bring about a significant improvement in the situation. the current shortcomings are partly due to the still predominant use of correspondents and the lack of appropriate interbank infrastructures. more efficient arrangements for transfers of funds have been introduced in recent years, but they are too fragmented and economies of scale are very limited. a prerequisite, therefore, for substantial improvement in the processing of small-value crossborder payments is certainly the need for the banking industry to apply common technical standards for interbank transfers of funds. however, this will probably not be enough. the banking industry also needs to significantly improve its internal procedures for processing cross-border payments, as well as its communication with customers, which in turn requires further automation and standardisation. in this connection, i would draw your attention to the standards agreed within the european banking standards committee, which i believe are of great importance. the ecb is responsible for organising meetings with all relevant parties to promote the application of these standards. once all the conditions for interbank processing and internal procedures are met, the banking industry should be able to significantly reduce the cost of cross-border transfers and reduce the execution time of transactions to the time required for a domestic transaction plus one day. the ecb expects that the banks in the euro area will achieve substantial improvements by 1 january 2002 at the latest. the bank will act as a catalyst for change; the commission also intends, with the assistance of the national central banks of the european system, to discuss these issues with the euro area banking industry in order to play a supporting and coordinating role in this respect. at the moment, there does not appear to be any justification for the ecb to be involved, as there are signs that the private sector is becoming more aware of the problem. however, the ecb will closely monitor developments in this area and will inform the european parliament and the general public of the progress made. taken previously. many have spoken here of independence. it is true that with the maastricht treaty those who, like myself, believed that price stability was a sine qua non without which sustainable artificially grow in the short term have lost. the spokesman for my group has said it very well and i shall not repeat it. however, given that we believe in this model, we also believe that steps must be taken to prevent this model from failing. firstly, there is the problem of transparency, which the rapporteur has mentioned with humour and discernment. we believe in the independence of the central bank, but it is much more independent than the bundesbank or the us federal reserve, because it is not the result of parliamentary action and it cannot be changed by parliamentary action, because it does not act with an economic government. that is why some have spoken of a kind of platonic aristocracy of a series of independent experts to whom we entrust monetary policy decisions, thinking - probably rightly - that money is too serious a thing for us politicians to concern ourselves with. if we want to avoid the failure of this model, we must therefore increase transparency measures. i fully support all the measures proposed by the rapporteur. secondly, there is the problem of the relationship between the central bank and the other european institutions. it has been said here that the priority objective is the fight against inflation, but this is not the only objective: we must talk, among other things, about an economic pole, responsibility, the international representation of the euro and the control of banking institutions at a time when we are witnessing major mergers between financial institutions.
- (es) mr president, mr president of the european central bank, ladies and gentlemen, we are holding this debate when the euro has already been in existence for nine months, in conditions which make it possible to ensure that its introduction has been a success, although only in the sense that the transition to the third stage of emu has taken place without major upheavals. since the central bank undoubtedly has a share in this success, we must congratulate its president, which we are doing. that said, we must insist on two or three questions. the first -
